title: Checks for argument-free @pytest.fixture() decorators with or without parentheses, depending on the lint.flake8-pytest-style.fixture-parentheses setting.
summary: If a @pytest.fixture() doesn't take any arguments, the parentheses are optional. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for pytest.fixture calls with positional arguments.
summary: For clarity and consistency, prefer using keyword arguments to specify fixture configuration. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.
message_templates: Configuration for fixture `{}` specified via positional args, use kwargs

title: Checks for pytest.fixture calls with scope="function".
summary: scope="function" can be omitted, as it is the default. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for pytest fixtures that do not return a value, but are not named with a leading underscore.
summary: By convention, fixtures that don't return a value should be named with a leading underscore, while fixtures that do return a value should not. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style, and removed it.
message_templates: Fixture `{}` does not return anything, add leading underscore

title: Checks for pytest fixtures that return a value, but are named with a leading underscore.
summary: By convention, fixtures that don't return a value should be named with a leading underscore, while fixtures that do return a value should not. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style, and removed it.
message_templates: Fixture `{}` returns a value, remove leading underscore

title: Checks for the type of parameter names passed to pytest.mark.parametrize.
summary: The argnames argument of pytest.mark.parametrize takes a string or a sequence of strings. For a single parameter, it's preferable to use a string. For multiple parameters, it's preferable to use the style configured via the lint.flake8-pytest-style.parametrize-names-type setting. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.
message_templates: Wrong type passed to first argument of `pytest.mark.parametrize`; expected {}

title: Checks for the type of parameter values passed to pytest.mark.parametrize.
summary: The argvalues argument of pytest.mark.parametrize takes an iterator of parameter values, which can be provided as lists or tuples. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.
message_templates: Wrong values type in `pytest.mark.parametrize` expected `{}` of `{}`

title: Checks for mocked calls that use a dummy lambda function instead of return_value.
summary: When patching calls, an explicit return_value better conveys the intent than a lambda function, assuming the lambda does not use the arguments passed to it. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for uses of assertion methods from the unittest module.
summary: To make use of pytest's assertion rewriting, a regular assert statement is preferred over unittest's assertion methods. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.
message_templates: Use a regular `assert` instead of unittest-style `{}`

title: Checks for pytest.raises calls without an expected exception.
summary: pytest.raises expects to receive an expected exception as its first argument. If omitted, the pytest.raises call will fail at runtime. The rule will also accept calls without an expected exception but with match and/or check keyword arguments, which are also valid after pytest version 8.4.0. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for pytest.raises calls without a match or check parameter.
summary: pytest.raises(Error) will catch any Error and may catch errors that are unrelated to the code under test. To avoid this, pytest.raises should be called with a match parameter (to constrain the exception message) or a check parameter (to constrain the exception itself). The exception names that require a match or check parameter can be configured via the lint.flake8-pytest-style.raises-require-match-for and lint.flake8-pytest-style.raises-extend-require-match-for settings. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.
message_templates: `pytest.raises({})` is too broad, set the `match` parameter or use a more specific exception

title: Checks for pytest.raises context managers with multiple statements.
summary: When a pytest.raises is used as a context manager and contains multiple statements, it can lead to the test passing when it actually should fail. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.
message_templates: `pytest.raises()` block should contain a single simple statement

title: Checks for incorrect import of pytest.
summary: For consistency, pytest should be imported as import pytest and its members should be accessed in the form of pytest.xxx.yyy for consistency Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.
message_templates: Incorrect import of `pytest`; use `import pytest` instead

title: Checks for duplicate test cases in pytest.mark.parametrize.
summary: Duplicate test cases are redundant and should be removed. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.285.
message_templates: Duplicate of test case at index {} in `pytest.mark.parametrize`

title: Checks for assert statements whose test expression is a falsy value.
summary: pytest.fail conveys the intent more clearly than assert falsy_value. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for pytest.fail calls without a message.
summary: pytest.fail calls without a message make it harder to understand and debug test failures. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for assert statements in except clauses.
summary: When testing for exceptions, pytest.raises() should be used instead of assert statements in except clauses, as it's more explicit and idiomatic. Further, pytest.raises() will fail if the exception is _not_ raised, unlike the assert statement. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.
message_templates: Found assertion on exception `{}` in `except` block, use `pytest.raises()` instead

title: Checks for assertions that combine multiple independent conditions.
summary: Composite assertion statements are harder to debug upon failure, as the failure message will not indicate which condition failed. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.
message_templates: Assertion should be broken down into multiple parts

title: Checks for pytest test functions that should be decorated with @pytest.mark.usefixtures.
summary: In pytest, fixture injection is used to activate fixtures in a test function. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.
message_templates: Fixture `{}` without value is injected as parameter, use `@pytest.mark.usefixtures` instead

title: Checks for pytest.yield_fixture usage.
summary: pytest.yield_fixture is deprecated. pytest.fixture should be used instead. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for unnecessary request.addfinalizer usages in pytest fixtures.
summary: pytest offers two ways to perform cleanup in fixture code. The first is sequential (via the yield statement), the second callback-based (via request.addfinalizer). Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for unnecessary yield expressions in pytest fixtures.
summary: In pytest fixtures, the yield expression should only be used for fixtures that include teardown code, to clean up the fixture after the test function has finished executing. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.
message_templates: No teardown in fixture `{}`, use `return` instead of `yield`

title: Checks for argument-free @pytest.mark.<marker>() decorators with or without parentheses, depending on the lint.flake8-pytest-style.mark-parentheses setting.
summary: If a @pytest.mark.<marker>() doesn't take any arguments, the parentheses are optional. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for unnecessary @pytest.mark.asyncio decorators applied to fixtures.
summary: pytest.mark.asyncio is unnecessary for fixtures. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for pytest.mark.usefixtures decorators applied to pytest fixtures.
summary: The pytest.mark.usefixtures decorator has no effect on pytest fixtures. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for @pytest.mark.usefixtures() decorators that aren't passed any arguments.
summary: A @pytest.mark.usefixtures() decorator that isn't passed any arguments is useless and should be removed. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for uses of exception-related assertion methods from the unittest module.
summary: To enforce the assertion style recommended by pytest, pytest.raises is preferred over the exception-related assertion methods in unittest, like assertRaises. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in v0.0.285.

title: Checks for parameters of test functions with default arguments.
summary: Such a parameter will always have the default value during the test regardless of whether a fixture with the same name is defined. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in 0.12.0.
message_templates: Test function parameter `{}` has default argument

title: Checks for pytest.warns calls without an expected warning.
summary: pytest.warns expects to receive an expected warning as its first argument. If omitted, the pytest.warns call will fail at runtime. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style. It is in preview.

title: Checks for pytest.warns calls without a match parameter.
summary: pytest.warns(Warning) will catch any Warning and may catch warnings that are unrelated to the code under test. To avoid this, pytest.warns should be called with a match parameter. The warning names that require a match parameter can be configured via the lint.flake8-pytest-style.warns-require-match-for and lint.flake8-pytest-style.warns-extend-require-match-for settings. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in 0.12.0.
message_templates: `pytest.warns({})` is too broad, set the `match` parameter or use a more specific warning

title: Checks for pytest.warns context managers with multiple statements.
summary: When pytest.warns is used as a context manager and contains multiple statements, it can lead to the test passing when it should instead fail. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pytest-style and made it stable in 0.12.0.
message_templates: `pytest.warns()` block should contain a single simple statement
